## Summary

Root cause: `docs/<locale>/index.md` (the VitePress home page) was hand-authored only for `hu` — every other locale had no home page file, so navigating to a locale root (e.g. `/ar/`) 404'd. VitePress has no built-in "fall back to English" for a missing locale route; a missing file is just a 404.

Fix:
- Added [docs/scripts/translate-home.ts](docs/scripts/translate-home.ts), which parses the hero/features frontmatter of the root `index.md`, translates `text:`/`tagline:`/`title:`/`details:` values through the existing translation-memory pipeline, and rewrites `link:` values with each locale's route prefix.
- Wired it into [docs/package.json](docs/package.json) as `docs:home:locales` (+ `:claude`/`:agy` variants) and into the `docs:locales:translate*` chains.
- Made `<locale>/index.md` a required file in [docs/scripts/check-locale-parity.ts](docs/scripts/check-locale-parity.ts) so a new locale added to `CANVAS_LOCALES` without a home page fails CI instead of silently 404ing.
- Ran the script (default `glossary` adapter) to generate `index.md` for all 43 non-root locales, including regenerating `hu`'s to match the same pipeline.

Run `vp run docs:home:locales:claude` (or `:agy`) locally for real translations instead of the glossary passthrough.
